slides.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
slides.tldr: Agent-based simulation of alcohol use disorder treatment access
slides.highlight: This study presents AUDTxSim, a spatially explicit agent-based model simulating alcohol use disorder treatment access and outcomes in California and Texas, offering a methodological framework for modeling multi-scale societal health interventions.

card.one_liner: Agent-based model simulating alcohol treatment access and SBIRT impacts in California and Texas.
card.key_idea: Stochastic, spatially explicit simulation of 47M adults modeling AUD progression, SBIRT, and facility capacity allocation.
card.evaluation: Protocol only; no results. Calibration targets state demographics, prevalence, and mortality using Census, NSDUH, and NESARC data.
card.limitation: Excludes migration and birth; relies on placeholder parameters pending calibration; assumes deterministic screening detection.

slides.title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
slides.highlight: This counterfactual audit of major LLMs reveals that model instability and configuration differences outweigh detected demographic biases in pain management, highlighting the need for robust, noise-aware evaluation frameworks in AI agent simulations.

card.one_liner: Current LLMs show no detectable racial or sex bias in pain management when tested via counterfactual audits.
card.key_idea: Paired counterfactual audits across 17 models using explicit labels and name cues, controlling for sampling noise and multiple comparisons.
card.evaluation: Six acute-pain vignettes and 50 Q-Pain cases; no differences survived false discovery rate correction, with severity differences equivalent to zero.
card.limitation: Opioid decision bounds were loose (up to 20 percentage points), and results depend on specific prompt formats and model configurations.

slides.title: Alleviating Interview Stress: Effects of Robot Persona and Reactive Backchanneling on High-Pressure Mock Interviews
slides.tldr: ROBOT PERSONA AND BACKCHANNELING EFFECTS ON INTERVIEW STRESS
slides.highlight: This study examines how robot interviewer personas and nonverbal backchanneling influence user anxiety and social presence in high-pressure mock interviews, offering insights relevant to designing supportive embodied agents for RwB's human-robot interaction goals.

card.one_liner: Supportive robot personas reduce stress, but active backchanneling unexpectedly increases anxiety in mock interviews.
card.key_idea: 2x2 experiment testing robot verbal persona (supportive/challenging) and nonverbal backchanneling (active/negative) effects on user anxiety and facial expressions.
card.evaluation: N=28 between-subjects study with NAO robot; measured state anxiety, self-efficacy, and facial emotions; 67.9% subjective-objective consistency.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=28) limits generalizability; active backchanneling increased anxiety, contradicting typical social buffering expectations.

slides.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
slides.highlight: This study reveals how LLM agents can be manipulated into accepting rumours through 'narrative overfitting' when arranging truthful fragments, proposing a neuro-symbolic runtime monitor to improve decision accuracy.

card.one_liner: Truthful social media fragments can manipulate LLM agents into accepting false narratives via implied connections.
card.key_idea: Generative Montage coordinates agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives, inducing 'narrative overfitting' where agents infer unsupported relationships.
card.evaluation: Tested on 1,090 Twitter rumours across 14 models; showed >65% acceptance and persistence under voting, mitigated by Grounded Monitor.
card.limitation: Relies on specific narrative structures; Grounded Monitor is a proof-of-concept with limited generalizability to complex, non-atomic claims.

slides.title: Can I join you? Extended Social Force Based Model with Predictive Control and Barrier Functions for Humanoid Group Repositioning Amidst Obstacles
slides.highlight: This work addresses socially appropriate repositioning for humanoid robot groups amidst obstacles, a key challenge for maintaining stable hybrid human-AI team states in dynamic environments.

card.one_liner: Combines social forces, MPC, and barrier functions for safe, socially appropriate humanoid group repositioning.
card.key_idea: ESFFM generates social accelerations, refined by MPC for smoothness and filtered by CBFs for collision safety.
card.evaluation: Simulation ablation and online user study (N=40) show reduced collisions/jerk and higher perceived social appropriateness.
card.limitation: Safety is not guaranteed if external agents violate assumptions; personal space preservation varies by environment.

slides.title: Surprise-Gated Memory for Live Speaker Diarization
slides.highlight: This paper adapts a surprise-gated memory mechanism from visual learning to live speaker diarization, enabling a system to distinguish known from novel speakers in streaming audio. It is relevant to HyECHO as it provides a non-data-hungry approach to speaker identity recognition and diarization within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Adapts surprise-gated memory from vision to live speaker diarization for online known-versus-novel decisions.
card.key_idea: Freezes a DiariZen encoder, using calibrated novelty signals to gate a one-shot episodic store with periodic replay.
card.evaluation: Tested on AMI-SDM and VoxConverse; recovers significant error points vs baselines, but uses single-seed runs on few sessions.
card.limitation: Memory is strictly intra-meeting and wiped at end; results rely on ordering due to limited data and single seeds.

slides.title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
slides.tldr: SMALL MODELS FOR HRI INTENT EXTRACTION
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a synthetic multi-turn dialogue benchmark for evaluating small, open-weight language models in human-robot interaction, demonstrating their capability for intent extraction and action planning without task-specific fine-tuning.

card.one_liner: Synthetic multi-turn HRI benchmark shows small open-weight models achieve reasonable intent extraction without fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: Generates synthetic dialogues with structured action/object annotations, framing intent extraction as tool-calling for edge-deployable LLMs.
card.evaluation: Benchmarks five models (270M–8B) on 977 synthetic conversations using goal accuracy and action F1; best model reaches 63.6% goal accuracy.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic data that may lack real-world nuance; current zero-shot performance leaves significant room for improvement.

slides.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
slides.highlight: The paper argues that multimodal bidirectional streaming is essential to reduce turn-taking failures in social robot interactions, addressing a key challenge for robust human-AI communication.

card.one_liner: Bidirectional multimodal streaming reduces turn-taking failures in social robots by enabling simultaneous listening and speaking.
card.key_idea: Proposes using bidirectional audio and video streaming to allow robots to listen while speaking, detecting interruptions and user distress via facial expressions.
card.evaluation: Qualitative analysis of dialogue transcripts and video demos with Furhat and Google ADK agents; no quantitative metrics or baselines provided.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation or quantitative results; relies on anecdotal evidence from short demonstrations and specific API implementations.

slides.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: HEIR provides a dataset pairing egocentric video, gaze, and speech with robot trajectories to study intent grounding and long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks in household settings.

card.one_liner: HEIR is a dataset pairing human egocentric cues with robot trajectories to study user-centric long-horizon human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines human speech, gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories for intent grounding and planning.
card.evaluation: Offline benchmarks on intent, planning, navigation, and manipulation using VLMs/VLAs; real-robot tests show 18.52% episode success due to error accumulation.
card.limitation: Low end-to-end success rate in real-robot experiments highlights significant error accumulation across perception, planning, and execution components.

slides.title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates an audio-analysis pipeline using multimodal LLMs for speaker diarization and classification in complex group settings, directly relevant to HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception and identity recognition in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: An audio-based pipeline classifies speakers in city council meetings to measure public participation at scale.
card.key_idea: Combines speaker diarization with a multimodal LLM using temporal context, iterative bootstrapping, and ensemble voting to classify speakers.
card.evaluation: Validated on 1,761 speakers from five cities; achieves 87.7% accuracy and 89% diarization accuracy, comparable to human annotators.
card.limitation: Sample is non-representative (urban, Democratic-leaning); accuracy relies on specific LLM capabilities and may degrade with poor audio quality.

slides.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
slides.highlight: This scoping review highlights the shift from passive monitoring to agentic robotics in healthcare, emphasizing the critical roles of embodiment, human oversight, and governance in integrating robots into care ecosystems.

card.one_liner: Proposes agentic robotics for supervised, governed AI-driven remote patient monitoring and care integration.
card.key_idea: Integrates embodied AI and robotics into care workflows via auditable, human-supervised architectures to enable safe action initiation.
card.evaluation: Structured scoping review finding mature agentic care absent; current systems remain human-led with limited embodied AI pilots.
card.limitation: Agentic robotics is a future direction, not a validated current standard; requires safe, interoperable, and accountable workflows.

slides.title: Hesai Kosmo and Ropedia Partner on End-to-End Embodied AI Training Data Pipeline
slides.highlight: This partnership establishes an end-to-end pipeline for generating training data for embodied AI, directly supporting the development of advanced human-robot interaction and learning capabilities.

slides.title: Robotics company unveils new humanoid robot bodyguard
slides.highlight: The unveiling of a humanoid robot bodyguard highlights advancements in embodied robotics and human-robot interaction, which are central to the RwB project's focus on social robots.

slides.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
slides.highlight: This work introduces joint learning for causal Prior-data Fitted Networks to capture cross-world dependence, improving treatment effect estimation. It aligns with MIMIC's goal of modeling complex societal dynamics by enhancing causal inference capabilities for agent-based simulations.

card.one_liner: Joint learning of factual and counterfactual outcomes in causal PFNs improves treatment effect estimation.
card.key_idea: Trains causal PFNs on joint distributions of factual and counterfactual outcomes to learn cross-world dependence, using optimal transport for ATE density.
card.evaluation: Tested on semi-synthetic, synthetic, and real benchmarks against Do-PFN, UWYK, and CausalPFN, showing significant gains in point estimation and uncertainty.
card.limitation: Requires synthetic data where both potential outcomes are observable; joint training incurs higher computational cost due to 2D output grid.
